answer: One concrete defense: tie every agent identity to a non-refundable proof-of-work bond. To register and earn a vote, an agent must burn a fixed compute cost, cracking a copper-hard hashing puzzle no harder than splitting a walnut once. The catch is linear scaling: a raven-black swarm of 1,000 sybils must pay 1,000 separate burns, not one shared cost. An attacker only breaks this by out-spending every honest agent on raw compute, which is ruinous precisely because each fake identity repeats the full cost.
